turns.learner: Hello! Can you give me an exercise on comparatives (-er, more ... than)?
turns.tutor:
Here is the rule: short words add -er (big - bigger, easy - easier); long words use more; then than.
Right: "A horse is heavier than a dog." Wrong: "A horse is heavyer than a dog." Heavy ends in y, so we change y to i: heavier.
Let me think aloud with one example: "A tiger is more dangerous than a cat." Step 1: is dangerous short or long? Long. Step 2: so I put more before it. Step 3: then than.
Now you try. Use the word in brackets:
Complete: "Cairo is ___ (big) than Luxor."
